cases.ambiguous_student_response: Predicts that Bulb 2 glows dimmer than Bulb 1 in a series circuit.

competing_explanations.name: Current Attenuation Model
competing_explanations.hypothesis: Student believes electric current is physically consumed or depleted as it passes through Bulb 1, so less current reaches Bulb 2.

competing_explanations.name: Voltage Exhaustion / Conflation
competing_explanations.hypothesis: Student acknowledges charge may be conserved, but believes 'voltage' is an energetic substance carried by current that is entirely spent inside the first resistor.

disambiguation_probe_item.stem: In the same series circuit of two identical bulbs, we now insert two ammeters: Ammeter X immediately before Bulb 1, and Ammeter Y immediately after Bulb 2 (between Bulb 2 and the negative battery terminal). What will the two ammeters read?

discriminating_options.text: Ammeter X reads higher than Ammeter Y (e.g. X = 0.6 A, Y = 0.3 A).
discriminating_options.cognitive_inference: Confirms Current Attenuation: the student explicitly models current loss along the loop.

discriminating_options.text: Ammeter X and Ammeter Y show the exact same current reading (X = Y = 0.4 A), but Bulb 2 is dimmer because voltage was used up by Bulb 1.
discriminating_options.cognitive_inference: Confirms Voltage Exhaustion: the student conserves current but conceptualizes voltage as a consumed substance.

discriminating_options.text: Ammeter X and Ammeter Y show identical readings, and both identical bulbs glow with the exact same brightness.

cases.ambiguous_student_response: Predicts that adding a parallel branch reduces the brightness of the first bulb.

competing_explanations.name: Constant Current Battery
competing_explanations.hypothesis: Student believes the battery delivers a fixed total amperage, which must now be partitioned between two branches.

competing_explanations.name: Parallel Resistance Addition
competing_explanations.hypothesis: Student believes adding another branch increases total resistance, choking the circuit.

disambiguation_probe_item.stem: A 10 V ideal battery is connected across Bulb 1. We connect Bulb 2 in parallel. An ammeter measures the total current leaving the battery positive terminal. What happens to the total battery current?

discriminating_options.text: The total battery current stays exactly the same as before, because a 10 V battery has a fixed current rating that cannot change.
The total battery current decreases, because having two resistors in the circuit creates more resistance to current flow than having only one.
The total battery current increases to twice its original value, while the current through Bulb 1 remains unchanged.
discriminating_options.cognitive_inference: Correct independent branch analysis under constant terminal voltage.

cases.ambiguous_student_response: States that an image of a candle flame cannot be seen if a white paper screen is removed from the focus of a convex lens.

competing_explanations.name: Screen Reification
competing_explanations.hypothesis: Student believes light rays only materialize into an image when stopped by an opaque diffusing surface.

competing_explanations.name: Virtual Image Ray Convergence Fallacy
competing_explanations.hypothesis: Student does not understand real vs virtual image definitions, assuming images are purely mental illusions inside the lens.

disambiguation_probe_item.stem: The white screen is removed. An observer positions their eye 20 cm further back along the optical axis, looking directly back towards the lens along the path of the converging/diverging rays. What will the observer see?

discriminating_options.text: The observer sees nothing at all, because without a screen, light rays continue indefinitely as invisible rays and cannot form an image in empty air.
discriminating_options.cognitive_inference: Isolates Screen Reification: observer cannot conceptualize an aerial real image entering the eye pupil.

discriminating_options.text: The observer sees a sharp, inverted, inverted image floating in space at the exact previous position of the screen, because the diverging rays from the real image point enter the observer's eye pupil.
discriminating_options.cognitive_inference: Correct scientific understanding of aerial image propagation.

discriminating_options.text: The observer sees an erect virtual image located inside the glass of the lens itself.

cases.ambiguous_student_response: Claims that a current-carrying wire placed in a magnetic field experiences zero deflection force.

competing_explanations.name: Charge Neutrality Misunderstanding
competing_explanations.hypothesis: Student reasons that because the wire is electrically neutral overall (equal protons and electrons), a magnet cannot interact with it.

competing_explanations.name: Collinear / Orientation Dependence Confusion
competing_explanations.hypothesis: Student misapplies the vector orientation rule, thinking force is zero because wire is perpendicular, or that force is parallel.

disambiguation_probe_item.stem: If the current-carrying wire is now rotated so that it is oriented strictly parallel to the magnetic field lines (angle = 0 degrees), what will happen to the magnetic force?

discriminating_options.text: The force becomes maximum, because the current is now aligned directly with the magnetic field lines.
discriminating_options.cognitive_inference: Isolates Collinear Force Fallacy: student assumes parallel alignment produces maximum interaction (like electric fields).

discriminating_options.text: The force remains zero, but for the same reason: an electrically neutral metal wire never experiences magnetic force regardless of orientation.
discriminating_options.cognitive_inference: Isolates Electrostatic Charge Conflation: rejects magnetic force on steady current based on electrostatic neutrality.

discriminating_options.text: The force becomes zero because F is proportional to sin(theta), and sin(0 deg) = 0, whereas in the perpendicular position the force was maximum.
discriminating_options.cognitive_inference: Correct vector cross-product understanding (F = I * L * B * sin(theta)).
